paragraphs.content: Freshly juiced fruit has become a basic dietary item — especially for busy, health-conscious consumers who can save time on making (and perhaps even chewing) their food without missing out on nutrients. Fruit juice also has been linked to claims that it can help you both lose weight and stay healthy. All of which, of course, has made it highly profitable. The global fruit and vegetable juices market was valued at $154 billion in 2016 and is expected to grow.

But is juicing really as healthy as we think? Most foods containing fructose—a naturally occurring sugar found in all fruits and fruit juices — don’t seem to have harmful effects as long as they’re not contributing to excess daily calories. This is because the fibre found in whole fruits is intact, and the sugar is contained within the fruit’s cells. It takes our digestive system a while to break these cells down and for fructose to enter the bloodstream.

But this is not the case with fruit juice. Unlike whole fruit, fruit juice has most of the fibre removed. This is why the fructose in fruit juices counts as ‘free sugars’ — which also include honey and the sugars added to foods. It’s recommended by the World Health Organisation that adults have no more than 30g of added sugar, the equivalent of 150ml of fruit juice, per day. The problem is that, with the fibre removed, fruit juice’s fructose is absorbed more quickly. Sudden increases in blood sugar cause the release of insulin (胰岛素) to bring it back down to a stable level. Over time, this mechanism can wear out increasing the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. In 2013, researchers analysed the health data of 100,000 people collected between 1986 and 2009 and found that fruit juice consumption was linked with increased risk of type 2 diabetes. Another study found a relationship between fruit juice and type 2 diabetes after following the diets and diabetes status of more than 70,000 nurses over 18 years. The researchers explain that the possible reason for this may partly have been the lack of the other components found in whole fruit, like fibre.

Juices containing vegetables can provide more nutrients and less sugar than juices made up of just fruit — but they still lack valuable fibre. Diets high in fibre have been linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure and diabetes, and it’s recommended adults consume 30g per day.

Aside from the link to type 2 diabetes, many studies agree that fruit juice is harmful if it contributes to an excess in calories. In an analysis of 155 studies, John Sievenpiper, associate professor at the University of Toronto’s Department of Nutritional Sciences, set out to understand if the associations between sugary soft drinks and health — including risk of diabetes and heart disease — were applicable to the food and drink we generally consume as part of a healthy diet. He compared studies looking into the effects of fructose-containing sugars with control diets free from or lower in these sugars. His aim? To isolate the effects of consuming too many calories from the effects of foods containing different sugars.

He found negative effects on blood sugar and insulin levels when food provided excess calories from sugars, including fruit juice. However, when the calories weren't in excess overall, there were some advantages to consuming whole fruit — and even fruit juice. Sievenpiper concludes that the recommended 150ml of fruit juice per day, which is an average serving, is reasonable. The paper concluded that foods containing fructose may have some small benefits for long-term blood sugar control when they don’t lead to over-consumption of calories. But when they do lead to too many calories, they risk raising blood sugar and insulin levels.

So while we know that fruit juice can cause diabetes if it’s part of a diet that has more calories overall, it's less clear how juice affects the long-term health of those who aren’t overweight. But we have a higher risk of consuming more than the recommended daily number of calories (around 2,000 for women and 2,500 for men) on the days we drink juice, according to research. Numerous studies have shown that drinking fruit juice doesn’t make us consume any less of other foods throughout the day.

As it is easy to consume large amounts of fruit juice quite quickly, extra calories are taken in. And extra calories can contribute to weight gain. One way we can improve the effects of fruit juice on our health is making sure we select ripe fruit to retain as much of its goodness as possible, according to Roger Clemens, professor of pharmaceutical (药物的) sciences at the University of Southern California.

Another reason for fruit juice’s recent popularity is the argument that it can help to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body. However, “the whole concept of a juice diet helping to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body is completely false,” says Clemens. “We consume compounds every day that may be poisonous and our bodies do a wonderful job of removing and eliminating anything harmful from our bodies.”

And juice isn’t a cure-all for getting your nutrients, either. “There are a lot of nutrients contained in the parts of the fruits, such as in apple skins, that are excluded when you juice them,” says Heather Ferris, a professor of medicine. “You end up with sugary water with some vitamins.”

Plus, she adds, it’s not an ideal way to reach the advised ‘five a day’. “People try to get five servings of fruit and vegetables per day and don’t realise this isn’t just about getting vitamins,” she says. “It’s also about reducing the amount of grain carbs (碳水化合物) and protein and fats in our diet, and increasing fibre.” So while fruit juice is better than no fruit at all, there are limits. It particularly comes with risks when we consume more than 150ml of free sugars per day, or when it puts us over our recommended calorie intake. It provides us with vitamins — but fruit juice is far from a quick fix.

We all take a little extra effort to look nice for special occasions. But most of us have conflicting feelings about dressing up and feel guilty about taking the time to focus on clothes. Science now suggests the right dress may give ourselves the extra edge in our professional and personal lives.

We hear sayings like “dress for the job you want, not the job you have”. Most people don’t really believe in them, but research into the impact of clothes on behavior now suggests that there may actually be a grain of truth in these sayings. Science says that the clothes we wear affect our behavior, our mood and even the way we interact with others because of the symbolic meaning that we assign to different types of clothing.

We consider some clothes to be powerful some to be fun, and so on. We even evaluate people whom we have just met based on their clothes. We also evaluate ourselves based on what we are wearing because of the way they make us feel. This means that the experience of wearing something affects our attitudes and our choice of behavior.

There’s a reason tailored jackets are associated with being “dressed for success”. It seems that wearing formal office wear puts us in the right frame of mind to conduct business. Wearing power clothing makes us feel more confident and even increases hormones needed for displaying dominance. This in turn helps us become better negotiators and abstract thinkers.

While a good suit works wonders for our performance in the boardroom, wearing formal wear isn’t a great idea when we want to socialize. Studies have found that people tend to be less open and less able to relax when they wear formal clothes.

On the other hand, a casual dress helps us become more friendly and creative. These findings support the idea of wearing business casuals on a Friday, since colleagues are most likely to take out time to socialize on the last work day of the week. I mean, who wants to hang out with people in their suits?

With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye. Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music. Granted, you will not typically see today's teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive.

The most major indicator of classical music’s importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies (旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music’s best works. Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic (交响乐的) orchestras have had on society’s taste in music.

A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form. The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least bit. In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself. Some of the world’s greatest hits have been parts of rock operas.

Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures. These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans.

Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, it is without doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come.

00:03:53,600 --> 00:03:58,040
the European and the UK Space Agencies.
欧洲和英国的航天局。

38
00:03:58,480 --> 00:04:02,620
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
问题 3 和 4 是基于你刚刚听到的新闻报道。

39
00:04:03,180 --> 00:04:08,080
Question 3. What do we learn from the news report about Tim Peake?
问题 3。从新闻报道中我们了解到了关于蒂姆·皮克的什么信息？

40
00:04:22,400 --> 00:04:29,180
Question 4. What does Tim Peake say about his work with the European Space Agency?
问题 4。蒂姆·皮克如何评价他在欧洲航天局的工作？

新闻报道 3。

00:04:46,440 --> 00:04:53,280
An Asda store in Wales is now home to five cats, after they wandered in and made themselves

comfortable.
生活得很惬意。

这家超市以其忠实的顾客而闻名，但现在却有了一种在过去一年里

45

that has appeared over the last year.
不断出现的另类“访客”。

46
00:05:03,100 --> 00:05:11,400
Regular shoppers at the supermarket are familiar with the sight of several cats, settling down in the shop aisles.
经常光顾这家超市的顾客对几只猫在商店走廊里安顿下来的景象已经习以为常了。

47
00:05:12,240 --> 00:05:19,660
The unusual situation started about 12 months ago, when one cat routinely started visiting the store.
这种情况始于大约 12 个月前，当时有一只猫开始经常光顾这家店。

48
00:05:20,540 --> 00:05:28,660
Local newspapers reported that puzzled customers posted on Facebook groups to try to find out if the cat was lost.
当地报纸报道称，困惑的顾客在 Facebook 群组里发帖，试图弄清楚这只猫是否走失了。

49
00:05:28,660 --> 00:05:35,080
But its owner assured the concerned customers, it was very much loved and fed at home.
但猫的主人向关心的顾客保证，它在家里非常受宠，且有充足的食物。

50
00:05:35,660 --> 00:05:37,960
It just enjoyed visiting the shop.
它只是喜欢逛店而已。

51
00:05:39,020 --> 00:05:44,380
Staff did their best to discourage the pet from hanging around, but instead of leaving
工作人员尽力阻止宠物在店里逗留，但它不仅没有离开

52
00:05:44,380 --> 00:05:48,300
and never coming back, it invited its friends around.
再也不回来，反而邀请了它的朋友们过来。

53
00:05:49,100 --> 00:05:54,240
There are now at least five different cats who come almost on a daily basis.
现在至少有五只不同的猫几乎每天都会来。

54
00:05:54,240 --> 00:06:01,140
They visit the store so much that staff have been forced to put up signs, asking their
由于它们来得太频繁，工作人员不得不贴出告示，要求

55

customers not to feed them.
顾客不要喂食它们。

56
00:06:30,460 --> 00:06:37,700

57
00:06:37,700 --> 00:06:38,640
in the store?

4
00:00:34,060 --> 00:00:35,420
Conversation 1
对话 1

5
00:00:35,420 --> 00:00:39,260
I've been thinking about moving off campus next semester.
我一直在考虑下学期搬到校外去住。

6
00:00:40,220 --> 00:00:42,300
Hmm, I don't know if that's a good idea.
嗯，我不知道这是否是个好主意。

7
00:00:42,820 --> 00:00:48,740
As your mother and I would worry about you living all by yourself in an apartment so far from home.
我和你妈会担心你一个人住在离家那么远的公寓里。

8
00:00:48,740 --> 00:00:53,040
And then there's the expense too. I'm not sure we can afford it.
而且还有开销问题。我不确定我们是否负担得起。

9
00:00:53,560 --> 00:00:55,640
Well, I wouldn't be alone actually.
嗯，其实我不是一个人住。

10
00:00:56,180 --> 00:01:00,000
Three of my friends from the dormitory would share the place with me.
宿舍里的三个朋友会和我合租。

11
00:01:00,400 --> 00:01:04,459
And with four of us, it wouldn't cost anymore than living in the dorm.
我们四个人一起分担，费用不会比住校内宿舍多。

12
00:01:05,180 --> 00:01:06,540
Are you sure about that?
你确定吗？

13
00:01:06,780 --> 00:01:11,160
Rents in big cities are high, and then there's the cost of electricity and gas.
大城市的房租很高，而且还有电费和燃气费。

14
00:01:11,460 --> 00:01:13,040
Have you factored those in?
你把这些都考虑进去了吗？

15
00:01:13,320 --> 00:01:17,220
We've budgeted for those, and for internet and transportation.
我们已经把这些预算进去了，还有网费和交通费。

16
00:01:17,820 --> 00:01:24,120
And, if we move far enough from the city center, the rent is low enough for us to afford
而且，如果我们搬到离市中心足够远的地方，房租就低到我们可以负担
 
17
00:01:24,120 --> 00:01:25,140
all of it.
所有费用。

18
00:01:25,460 --> 00:01:27,580
What about the commutes to and from campus?
那往返学校的通勤呢？

19
00:01:28,060 --> 00:01:32,680
It sounds like you'll be wasting several hours every day on the road instead of studying.
听起来你每天会把好几个小时浪费在路上，而不是学习。

20
00:01:33,400 --> 00:01:38,160
It's about an hour to campus, but there's no reason I can't study on the bus.
去学校大约需要一小时，但我没理由不能在公交车上学习。

21
00:01:38,680 --> 00:01:43,720
After all, I did that during high school, and my commute was even longer then.
毕竟我高中时就是这么做的，那时的通勤时间甚至更长。

22
00:01:43,720 --> 00:01:50,900
That's true, but I'm not sure why you want to leave campus and go through all that trouble when the cost is the same.
这倒是事实，但我不确定既然花费一样，你为什么想搬离校区去费那个劲。

23
00:01:51,300 --> 00:02:05,060
For a lot of reasons, we'd have a kitchen so we could cook ourselves, and we'd each have our own bedroom, where we could study, instead of going to the library, we'd just have more space and privacy.
有很多原因，我们会有厨房可以自己做饭，而且每个人都有独立的卧室可以学习，不用再去图书馆，我们的空间和隐私会更多。

24
00:02:05,840 --> 00:02:11,600
I'm not convinced that the benefits are greater than the disadvantages, but I'll discuss this with you another time.
我并不觉得利大于弊，但我会再找时间跟你讨论这个。

25
00:02:11,600 --> 00:02:17,380
Questions 8-11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
问题 8-11 是基于你刚刚听到的对话。

26
00:02:18,300 --> 00:02:23,360
Question 8. What has the woman been thinking of doing next semester?
问题 8。这位女士一直在考虑下学期做什么？

27
00:02:37,540 --> 00:02:42,920
Question 9. What does the man suggest the woman take into consideration?
问题 9。这位男士建议女士考虑什么？

28
00:02:57,580 --> 00:03:04,140
Question 10. What does the woman say she did during high school?
问题 10。这位女士说她高中时做了什么？

29
00:03:16,640 --> 00:03:21,980
Question 11. What does the man say he'll do at the end of the conversation?
问题 11。这位男士在对话结束时说他会做什么？

30
00:03:37,880 --> 00:03:42,480
Good morning. I'm looking for a present for my nephew, Lawrence.
早上好。我想给我的侄子劳伦斯挑一件礼物。

31
00:03:43,200 --> 00:03:45,480
Hi. Do you have anything in mind?
你好。你有什么心仪的选项吗？

32
00:03:45,480 --> 00:03:52,320
I'm not sure. No. Do you know what boys aged around 10 typically like?
不确定。不知道。你知道 10 岁左右的男孩通常喜欢什么吗？

33
00:03:53,140 --> 00:03:58,560
For that age group, our biggest seller this year has been this action figure. It's called
针对那个年龄段，我们今年卖得最好的是这个动作玩偶。它叫
 
34
00:03:58,560 --> 00:04:01,000
Bobo Man and it's incredibly popular.
“波波超人（Bobo Man）”，它非常受欢迎。

35
00:04:01,460 --> 00:04:02,600
Does it do anything?
它有什么功能吗？

36
00:04:03,200 --> 00:04:09,040
Not by itself. It has no batteries if that's what you mean. There's a Bobo Man cartoon,
它自己不会动。如果你是指这个的话，它不需要电池。有一部《波波超人》动画片，
 
37
00:04:09,040 --> 00:04:14,500
popular amongst young children you see, and this toy is the lead character from the show.
在小孩子里很流行，这个玩具就是剧中的主角。

38
00:04:15,200 --> 00:04:21,620
Oh, I understand now. I've never heard of it, but I do know little Lawrence loves cartoons.
噢，我明白了。我没听说过这个，但我确实知道小劳伦斯爱看动画片。

39
00:04:22,560 --> 00:04:26,540
Do you have any other popular toys? Perhaps something educational?
你还有其他受欢迎的玩具吗？也许是一些有教育意义的？

40
00:04:27,360 --> 00:04:32,500
Yes, of course. Right over here we have dozens of puzzles for children of all ages.
当然有。这边有几十种适合各年龄段孩子的拼图。

41
00:04:33,140 --> 00:04:38,840
They are fun, great for exercising the mind, and can be played either alone or in groups.
它们很有趣，能锻炼大脑，既可以一个人玩，也可以成群玩。

42
00:04:38,840 --> 00:04:45,720
I like this sort of idea. Lawrence has a sister who is slightly older, so maybe a game
我喜欢这种想法。劳伦斯有一个大一点的姐姐，所以也许一个
 
43
00:04:45,720 --> 00:04:47,740
that they can play together would be good.
能让他们一起玩的游戏会很好。

44
00:04:48,600 --> 00:04:53,660
What do you think of battleships then? It's a total classic. It has been around since
那你觉得“海战棋（Battleships）”怎么样？这绝对是经典。它从
 
45
00:04:53,660 --> 00:04:55,420
the 1930s.
20世纪30年代就有了。

46
00:04:55,600 --> 00:04:58,260
Oh yeah, we had one of those when growing up.
噢，对，我们小时候就玩过那个。

47
00:04:58,600 --> 00:05:04,620
Of course you did. Everyone did. And kids enjoy it just as much today as you and I did
当然玩过，大家都玩过。现在的孩子和我们小时候一样喜欢它。
 
48
00:05:04,620 --> 00:05:07,940
when we were young. Some games just never get old.
有些游戏永远不会过时。

49
00:04:07,940 --> 00:05:15,740
I suppose you are right. I have fond memories playing battleship when it was raining outside and we had to stay indoors.
我想你是对的。我有很多美好的回忆，以前下雨天待在室内就玩海战棋。

50
00:05:15,740 --> 00:05:18,460
That's decided then. How much?
那就定这个了。多少钱？

51
00:05:19,340 --> 00:05:21,880
19 pounds and 90 pence please.
请付 19 英镑 90 便士。

52
00:05:22,280 --> 00:05:25,520
There you are. Have a nice day. Thank you. You too.
给你。祝你有愉快的一天。谢谢，你也是。

53
00:05:26,360 --> 00:05:31,159
Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
问题 12-15 是基于你刚刚听到的对话。

54
00:05:31,600 --> 00:05:34,500
Question 12. What is the woman doing?
问题 12。这位女士正在做什么？

55
00:05:48,620 --> 00:05:50,060
Question 13.
问题 13。

56
00:05:50,920 --> 00:05:54,600
How does the man describe Bobo Man the action figure?
这位男士如何描述“波波超人”动作玩偶？

57
00:06:08,800 --> 00:06:14,920
Question 14. What kind of game does the woman think would be good for Lawrence?
问题 14。这位女士认为什么样的游戏对劳伦斯有好处？

58
00:06:28,920 --> 00:06:35,060
Question 15. What do we learn from the conversation about the game battleships?
问题 15。关于海战棋游戏，我们从对话中了解到了什么？

没问题，这是为您翻译并整理后的 SRT 对照格式。这部分包含大学英语四级（CET-4）听力理解第三部分（Section C）的三篇短文及其问题：

---

1
00:00:01,180 --> 00:00:16,880
Section C, directions. In this section, you will hear three passages. At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions. Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
第三节，说明。在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。在每篇短文结束时，你将听到三到四个问题。短文和问题都只播放一遍。

2
00:00:16,880 --> 00:00:32,280
After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
听完问题后，你必须从标记为 A、B、C 和 D 的四个选项中选出最佳答案。然后在答题卡 1 上相应的字母中心划一条单线进行涂黑。

3
00:00:33,540 --> 00:00:40,780
Passage 1. We assume that if we offer our customers more choices, then they'll be more likely to buy our products.
短文 1。我们假设如果向顾客提供更多选择，他们就更有可能购买我们的产品。

4
00:00:40,780 --> 00:00:47,840
But here's the paradox of choice. If a person is presented with too many choices, they are actually less likely to buy.
但这就是“选择悖论”：如果一个人面对太多的选择，他们实际购买的可能性反而会降低。

5
00:00:47,840 --> 00:00:55,300
In 2012, psychologists published a study about jams. On a regular day at a local food market,
2012 年，心理学家发表了一项关于果酱的研究。在当地食品市场的一个普通日子里，

6
00:00:55,300 --> 00:01:02,400
people would find a display table with 24 different kinds of jams.
人们会看到一个摆放着 24 种不同果酱的展示台。

7
00:01:02,400 --> 00:01:10,060
Then, on another day, at that same food market, people were given only six different types of jam choices.
然后，在另一天，在同一个市场，人们只得到了 6 种不同果酱的选择。

8
00:01:10,060 --> 00:01:17,240
Guess which display table led to more sales? The study found that while the bigger display table created more interest,
猜猜哪个展示台带来的销量更多？研究发现，虽然较大的展示台引起了更多关注，

9
00:01:17,240 --> 00:01:23,180
people were almost 10 times less likely to purchase a jar of jam than in the case of the smaller display.
但人们购买果酱的可能性比在较小展示台的情况下低了近 10 倍。

10
00:01:23,180 --> 00:01:30,200
Customer satisfaction takes a hit as well. In the study, the bigger display of jams leads to lower customer satisfaction than the smaller display.
顾客满意度也受到了影响。研究中，果酱展示越多，顾客的满意度反而比展示少时更低。

11
00:01:30,200 --> 00:01:37,020
In an extensive study published in 2015, researchers analyzed a total of 99 choice studies
在 2015 年发表的一项广泛研究中，研究人员分析了总共 99 项关于选择的研究，

12
00:01:37,020 --> 00:01:44,140
and specifically looked at those cases in which reducing choices helped to boost sales.
并专门研究了那些减少选择有助于提高销量的案例。

13
00:01:44,140 --> 00:01:51,460
They found four rules that motivate consumers to buy: when people want to make a quick and easy choice,
他们发现了促使消费者购买的四条规则：当人们想要做出快速简便的选择时；

14
00:01:51,460 --> 00:01:58,940
when the product is complex, when it's difficult to compare alternatives and when consumers don't have clear preferences.
当产品很复杂时；当难以比较替代品时；以及当消费者没有明确偏好时。

15
00:01:58,940 --> 00:02:15,040
So as you can see, when it comes to choices, less is more.
所以如你所见，在选择这件事上，少即是多。

16
00:02:15,720 --> 00:02:26,500
Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
问题 16 至 18 是基于你刚刚听到的短文。

17
00:02:21,180 --> 00:02:26,500
Question 16. What do we learn from the passage about the paradox of choice?
问题 16。关于“选择悖论”，我们从短文中了解到了什么？

18
00:02:40,220 --> 00:02:48,260
Question 17. What did the psychologists want to find out in their 2012 study about Jams?
问题 17。心理学家在 2012 年关于果酱的研究中想探究什么？

19
00:03:02,020 --> 00:03:08,740
Question 18. What is the finding of an extensive study published in 2015?
问题 18。2015 年发表的那项广泛研究的发现是什么？

20
00:03:23,600 --> 00:03:30,120
Passage 2. The New Year has come and gone, and many may have already forgotten what they had resolved to do on January 1.
短文 2。新年来了又走，许多人可能已经忘记了他们在 1 月 1 日下定的决心。

21
00:03:30,120 --> 00:03:38,640
But if that resolution was to volunteer more, now is the best time to start.
但如果那个决心是多做志愿者，那么现在就是开始的最佳时机。

22
00:03:39,720 --> 00:03:46,220
Volunteering can drop after the holiday season, and by February, some organizations lack the volunteers they had in surplus just a month ago.
假期过后，志愿服务可能会减少。到了二月，一些机构甚至缺乏一个月前还过剩的志愿者。

23
00:03:50,580 --> 00:03:57,820
According to one survey, only 26% of Americans volunteer, despite reports that many Americans view volunteering as worthwhile.
根据一项调查，只有 26% 的美国人参加志愿活动，尽管有报道称许多美国人认为志愿服务是值得的。

24
00:04:00,800 --> 00:04:02,140
Why such a disconnect?
为什么会有这样的脱节？

25
00:04:02,960 --> 00:04:07,360
Most people cite time and conflicting work schedules as major barriers.
大多数人将时间限制和工作安排冲突列为主要障碍。

26
00:04:08,220 --> 00:04:13,820
But employees and employers would actually benefit if companies made employee volunteering part of the job.
但如果公司将员工志愿服务作为工作的一部分，员工和雇主实际上都会受益。

27
00:04:13,820 --> 00:04:21,079
Researchers have found donating our time and talent to others can lower blood pressure, boost happiness, and improve mental and physical health.
研究人员发现，向他人捐赠时间和才华可以降低血压，提升幸福感，并改善身心健康。

28
00:04:25,740 --> 00:04:31,200
Studies have also linked employee volunteer programs with more productive employees.
研究还将员工志愿服务计划与更高的生产力联系起来。

29
00:04:32,020 --> 00:04:38,900
With so much emphasis on employee wellness these days, company volunteer programs could be the perfect 2025 resolution.
现在大家如此强调员工福祉，公司志愿服务计划可能是 2025 年完美的决心目标。

30
00:04:38,900 --> 00:04:46,820
But for volunteering to benefit employees and the workplace, the entire organization needs to be involved.
但为了让志愿服务惠及员工和职场，整个组织都需要参与其中。

31
00:04:46,820 --> 00:04:53,640
By allowing employees to donate their time during work hours, the workplace becomes an outlet for personal fulfillment, without affecting personal time.
通过允许员工在工作时间内捐赠时间，职场变成了个人成就感的出口，且不占用个人时间。

32
00:05:00,340 --> 00:05:07,100

33

00:06:25,860 --> 00:06:34,100
The vast majority of the UK's 200,000 tonnes of retail sector annual food waste comes from supermarkets.
英国零售业每年产生的 20 万吨食物浪费中，绝大部分来自超市。

40
00:06:34,100 --> 00:06:39,900
But it's a problem that impacts independent luxury food suppliers too.
但这也是一个影响独立高级食品供应商的问题。

41
00:06:40,200 --> 00:06:41,520
The scale is small. It's estimated at less than 1% of the UK's food waste total.
虽然规模较小，估计不到英国食物浪费总量的 1%。

42
00:06:48,040 --> 00:06:51,220
But the quality from these suppliers is high.
但这些供应商提供的产品质量很高。

43
00:06:51,780 --> 00:06:57,740
Everything, from specialist cheeses to sought-after coffee beans, gets thrown away every day in the current food system.
在目前的食品体系中，从特制奶酪到备受青睐的咖啡豆，每天都有各种产品被扔掉。

44
00:06:59,760 --> 00:07:04,840
This is where French entrepreneur Sophie Andre comes in.
这就是法国企业家索菲·安德烈发挥作用的地方。

45
00:07:05,220 --> 00:07:12,440
In 2016, she moved to London and began by setting up a business delivering luxury handmade food across the city.
2016 年，她搬到伦敦，开始创办一家在全市配送高级手工食品的公司。

46
00:07:14,720 --> 00:07:18,120
"Food delivery seems to be a big thing here," she says.
她说：“送餐服务在这里似乎是一件大事。”

47
00:07:18,720 --> 00:07:21,720
"So, I started delivering products by bicycle."
“于是，我开始用自行车配送产品。”

48
00:07:22,300 --> 00:07:27,660
Talking with local producers, I learned that a small part of the production is sometimes wasted due to problems with size or shape,
通过与当地生产商交谈，我了解到有时一小部分产品会因为尺寸或形状问题被浪费，

49
00:07:27,660 --> 00:07:33,960
but the quality of the products remains unchanged.
但产品的品质保持不变。

50
00:07:35,100 --> 00:07:40,940
Unlike many food waste projects that have sprung up in recent years, the idea is not simply to redistribute waste food but to provide a high-quality product.
与近年来涌现的许多食物浪费项目不同，她的想法不仅仅是重新分配浪费的食物，而是提供高质量的产品。

51
00:07:45,620 --> 00:07:51,840
Andre's company, Elisia, offers breakfast and snacks specifically aimed at business meetings and events.
安德烈的公司 Elisia 提供专门针对商务会议和活动的早餐和零食。

52
00:07:52,860 --> 00:08:00,740
Elisia uses waste products to create simple, natural, straightforward meals and snacks.
Elisia 利用（因外观等原因产生的）剩余产品来制作简单、天然、直接的膳食和零食。

53
00:08:01,500 --> 00:08:04,700
Perhaps unlike other waste food, the supply is regular.
也许与其他浪费的食物不同，这种供应是定期的。

54
00:08:05,620 --> 00:11:00,600
Suppliers will always have a certain amount of surplus, so the menus remain regular too. Andre believes this benefits both her business and her customers.
供应商总会有一定数量的余量，因此菜单也能保持固定。安德烈认为这不仅有利于她的生意，也有利于她的顾客。
